cv-ff8c208f.stem: Which chamber forms most of the sternocostal (anterior) surface of the heart?
cv-ff8c208f.explanation: Because the heart is rotated to the left, its anterior surface is formed mostly by the right ventricle; the right border by the right atrium, the left border by the left ventricle (and left auricle), the apex by the left ventricle and the base (posterior surface) by the left atrium. Lying close to the sternum, the right ventricle is the chamber most often injured in penetrating chest wounds.

cv-e4391593.stem: A patient with mitral stenosis develops difficulty swallowing and hoarseness. Enlargement of which chamber best explains these symptoms?
cv-e4391593.explanation: The left atrium forms the base of the heart and lies directly in front of the oesophagus. When it enlarges it compresses the oesophagus (dysphagia) and can stretch the left recurrent laryngeal nerve (Ortner syndrome). Because of the same relationship, transoesophageal echocardiography shows the left atrium best.

cv-241ef31a.stem: The fossa ovalis in the right atrium is the remnant of which fetal structure?
cv-241ef31a.explanation: In the fetus blood passes from the right to the left atrium through the foramen ovale. At birth the left atrial pressure rises, the septum primum is pressed against the septum secundum and closes the opening, leaving the fossa ovalis. In about a quarter of people a probe-patent opening (PFO) remains.

cv-03099d00.stem: Which structures bound Koch's triangle, which marks the position of the atrioventricular (AV) node?
options: Septomarginal trabecula, anterior papillary muscle and pulmonary valve
Fossa ovalis, limbus and opening of the inferior vena cava
Anterior cusp of the mitral valve, aortic valve and membranous septum
Crista terminalis, opening of the superior vena cava and auricle
Tendon of Todaro, septal cusp of the tricuspid valve and opening of the coronary sinus
cv-03099d00.explanation: Koch's triangle lies on the septal wall of the right atrium. The AV node sits at its apex; it is an important landmark for protecting the conducting system in cardiac surgery and ablation.

cv-29f558d6.stem: In the right ventricle, which structure runs from the interventricular septum to the base of the anterior papillary muscle and carries the right bundle branch?
cv-29f558d6.explanation: The moderator band carries part of the right bundle branch by a short route to the anterior papillary muscle, so that the papillary muscle contracts in time before the tricuspid valve closes. It also limits overdistension of the ventricle.

cv-db0c2ed6.stem: Which statement about the areas where the heart valves are best heard is correct?
options: Mitral valve – left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line (apex)
Aortic valve – left 2nd intercostal space, sternal border
Mitral valve – right 4th intercostal space, sternal border
Tricuspid valve – left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line
Pulmonary valve – right 2nd intercostal space, sternal border
cv-db0c2ed6.explanation: The areas follow the direction of blood flow rather than the anatomical position of the valves: aortic in the right 2nd space, pulmonary in the left 2nd space (sternal border), tricuspid at the lower left sternal border (4th–5th space) and mitral at the apex (left 5th space, midclavicular line).

cv-0b0d9052.stem: A patient with chest pain has ST elevation in the inferior leads (II, III, aVF) and second-degree AV block on the ECG. Which artery is most likely occluded?
cv-0b0d9052.explanation: In most people the diaphragmatic (inferior) surface of the heart is supplied by the posterior interventricular branch of the right coronary artery. Because the AV nodal artery also arises from the RCA in about 80–90% of cases, inferior MI is often accompanied by bradycardia and AV block.

cv-b34c730f.stem: Which artery supplies the anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum?
cv-b34c730f.explanation: The septal branches of the LAD supply the anterior 2/3 of the septum (including most of the left bundle branch) and the PDA the posterior 1/3. The LAD is the most frequently occluded coronary artery and causes extensive anterior infarcts.

cv-f11807d6.stem: How is 'right dominance' of the coronary circulation defined?
options: By the conus artery arising from the right aortic sinus
By the posterior interventricular branch arising from the right coronary artery
By the right coronary artery being larger
By the sinoatrial nodal artery arising from the right coronary artery
By the right ventricle being larger
cv-f11807d6.explanation: Dominance is defined by the source of the PDA, which supplies the posterior surface of the heart and the posterior part of the septum. About 70% of people are right-dominant; in left dominance the PDA arises from the circumflex artery.

cv-f1cfdd20.stem: Which artery does the great cardiac vein accompany?
cv-f1cfdd20.explanation: The great cardiac vein rises with the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove, turns into the left AV groove and drains into the coronary sinus. The middle cardiac vein runs with the PDA and the small cardiac vein with the right marginal artery. The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium.

cv-0b3efcf0.stem: Where is the natural pacemaker of the heart (sinoatrial node) located?
options: In the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava, at the upper end of the crista terminalis
In the outflow tract of the right ventricle
At the apex of Koch's triangle
In the left atrium at the openings of the pulmonary veins
In the membranous part of the interventricular septum
cv-0b3efcf0.explanation: The SA node lies just under the epicardium at the junction of the SVC and the right atrium and in about 60% of cases is supplied by the right coronary artery. The impulse travels from the atria to the AV node and through the bundle of His and its branches to the ventricles.

cv-0cef8d2c.stem: In cardiac surgery, which space allows a finger to be passed behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk so that a clamp can be placed?
cv-0cef8d2c.explanation: The transverse sinus lies between the aorta and pulmonary trunk in front and the SVC and pulmonary veins behind. It is used in bypass operations to control the great arteries together. The oblique sinus is the blind pocket behind the left atrium.

cv-f911d80e.stem: A patient stabbed in the chest has hypotension, distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds (Beck's triad). Which approach is most often used for pericardiocentesis?
options: The angle between the xiphoid process and the left costal margin (subxiphoid approach)
Right 5th intercostal space, anterior axillary line
Left 8th intercostal space, posterior axillary line
cv-f911d80e.explanation: In cardiac tamponade blood in the pericardial cavity prevents the heart from filling. The needle is directed from the subxiphoid region towards the left shoulder; this route stays away from the pleura and the coronary arteries.

cv-43207aff.stem: Why is the pain of pericarditis referred to the tip of the shoulder?
options: Because the pericardium is supplied by intercostal nerves
Because sensation from the fibrous and parietal serous pericardium is carried by the phrenic nerve (C3–C5)
Because the sympathetic afferents of the heart enter T1–T4
Because the pericardium receives fibres from the brachial plexus
Because the visceral pericardium is supplied by the vagus nerve
cv-43207aff.explanation: The parietal pericardium has somatic sensation carried by the phrenic nerve; the pain is referred to the tip of the shoulder, the C4 dermatome. The pain of myocardial ischaemia, by contrast, travels with sympathetic afferents to T1–T4 and is referred to the inner side of the arm.

cv-b5bdf8d5.stem: Which two structures does the ligamentum arteriosum connect?
options: Aortic arch and left subclavian artery
Pulmonary trunk and superior vena cava
Right pulmonary artery and azygos vein
Left pulmonary artery and aortic arch
cv-b5bdf8d5.explanation: The ligamentum arteriosum is the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus; it joins the origin of the left pulmonary artery to the underside of the aortic arch. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under the aortic arch lateral to this ligament.
